summary: I sent the exact prompt. Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the Services page and the vendored kit, then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (408 lines). The page code in the plan builds the Deploys page from the kit: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the hand-written markup from services.js. No tracked files were changed. The agent asked no clarifying questions, and I didn't need to say anything after the first prompt.
reasoning: All four criteria are met. The skill was invoked and the plan file exists. The plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField from the vendored kit instead of hand-writing table and select markup. git shows no changes to any tracked or untracked non-ignored file.

observations.description: Onboarding: on both the trust-folder screen and the bypass-permissions screen, the option selected by default is "No, exit". Pressing Enter by reflex would quit.

While planning, the agent ran `npm test` in the real repo. It also built a scratch copy of the repo with `git archive` in a temp dir and ran the plan's code there (it reported "all 30 tests passed"). The working tree was left untouched, but running code goes beyond pure planning. Some users who asked only for a plan might not expect it.

The agent ran a Codex review-gate preflight and then wrote an entry to an 'ungated ledger' ("I logged the skipped review in the ungated ledger"). The plugin's review-gate plumbing shows up in a planning-only request, which may confuse users.

Good: the summary called out the spec choices it had to make itself, such as the default sort, the duration format ("0m 45s", with no hours unit) and the text shown when there are no deploys at all. It also explained why it read "behave as on the Services page" as being about behavior rather than markup.

Possible edge-case bug in the plan's code: formatDuration uses Math.round on seconds and then `seconds % 60`. If finishedAt comes before startedAt (bad data), the result would show a negative value. Minor.

criteria.evidence: Screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". It was also the first tool_use in the session log: "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans".

`ls docs/*/plans/` returned 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gave 408 lines. Before I sent anything, the agent's final message on screen said it was waiting: "When you've read the plan, tell me to go ahead..."

criteria.criterion: Plan builds table and env filter with kit dataTable and selectField
criteria.evidence: Plan lines 184-189 import from '#kit/badge', '#kit/empty', '#kit/filter-bar', '#kit/page-header', '#kit/select' and '#kit/table'. The renderDeploys code calls `filterBar({ ... fields: [ selectField({ name: 'env', ...}) ], keep: { sort, dir } })` and `dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort, sortHref, empty: emptyState(...) })`. grep for `<table` or `<select` found them only in test assertions (lines 127 and 156), never in page code. Line 9 of the plan states: "It does **not** copy the hand-written table, sort links, form and `.pill` markup from `src/pages/services.js`."

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public/vendor/package.json changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` printed nothing. `git status --porcelain --ignored` showed only `!! docs/`, because docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored. `git diff HEAD --stat` was empty and HEAD is still cd21dc5. In the session log, the only Write/Edit calls were on the plan file. The agent tested its code by running `git archive HEAD` into a mktemp scratch dir, not in the repo.
